Thanks again Madam Chair this report as you mentioned is in response to a Councilor inquiry from the meeting of city council that was held on October 25, 2023.
The inquiry includes questions on the process and approach used to establish the location of new orange utility pedestal boxes.
The level of citizen engagement involved and who is financially responsible to relocate a pedestal if it interferes with future development.
Pedestal locations are determined by engineering design infrastructure conflict avoidance and to comply with existing property boundaries.
Whenever possible, pedestals are located at the corner of properties or adjacent to other infrastructure such as existing polls to minimize the impact for all customers.
The overall goal is to achieve the lowest insulation cost while meeting technical requirements as well as minimizing the impact for all customers.
If a pedestal needs to be located on private property, sastoon light and power engages with the land owner for their approval.
However, if a pedestal can be located in the public right away, typically there is no engagement with adjacent property owners.
However, for large neighborhood wide electrical upgrade projects, sastoon light and power does inform the neighborhood.

Each reducing a policy or process that requires engagement with adjacent land owners prior to the insulation may have challenges due to conflicts between neighbors where neither wants the infrastructure adjacent to their property or where there are no alternative locations to offer, resulting in project timelines and cost increases.
In addition, minor changes are sometimes required during construction and reengaging with property owners result in further delays and increase costs.
Approximately 60 pedestals were installed over the past two years and there have been two concerns brought to our attention.
The cost to install a new pedestal is approximately $11,000 and is funded directly from the electrical utility.
The cost to relocate a pedestal is paid for by the customer requesting the relocation and cost approximately $5,000.
This is an information report that I am chair and our team is available to answer any questions that the committee may have.
